answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks that independent peers later verify, with rewards locked until several unrelated reviewers attest to the result. A new identity has no track record, so it must first do low-value work and build trust; splitting into many sybils does not multiply influence because reviewers are sampled across established identities. This resembles a prism sorting a gale of claims: an opal-bright fake still costs the attacker time, labor, and collateral before it can sway decisions.
